_: AUTHORED. This file holds attention and nothing else.
Existence, title and DONE come from the origin — the README's roadmap checkbox,
a test case's status marker, an operations record's frontmatter. `done` is not a
legal value here; tick it at the origin instead. Every id below must resolve, so
run `python3 tracker/tools/build_tracker.py --ids` rather than guessing one.
Keys per item: state, note, since, blocked_by, lane.

ops:duns.note: Hold lifted 2026-08-19: file as a sole proprietorship. Steps + the exact details checklist are in this record (§How to file) — search Apple's D-U-N-S lookup first, the request is free, details must match the GST certificate exactly, and the verification email arrives from D&B's domain (check the sender). Pay nobody.

ops:dlt-entity.note: Gates every SMS the platform will ever send. Needs PAN + GST certificate in hand.

ops:meta-business.note: Gates WhatsApp entirely. Free, and the whole WABA chain waits behind it.

ops:play-console.note: Organisation or personal is undecided, and it changes what this account IS — a new personal account carries Google's closed-test requirement (a dozen testers before production).

ops:apple-developer.note: Same undecided enrolment path. Also the account that unlocks APNs, so iOS push waits behind it either way.

ops:bank-account.note: Gates UPI PSP onboarding, which is itself weeks.

ops:gcp-maps.note: Restricted key, not an open one. Nothing downstream is blocked by it, but it costs an hour.

ops:firebase.note: Free, five minutes, and push on every platform waits on it.

ops:owner-store-account-entity.note: Blocks the D-U-N-S, and therefore both store accounts. Ask Apple and Google directly rather than inferring from docs written for companies — a proprietorship has no legal personality separate from its proprietor. If the answer is individual-only, ~4 weeks come off the critical path and the apps publish under a personal name.

ops:accountant-hsn-digits.note: The tightest dependency in the whole plan — needed W7, and the only one with no service level on the other side.

ops:owner-catalogue-export.note: Everything about the real catalogue is waiting on this. The 60 products in the prototypes are demo data; nobody here has seen the shop's actual range, its size, or whether it already carries HSN codes.

ops:accountant-hsn-values.note: Ask in the same conversation as the digit count. An HSN has no check digit, so a wrong one is invisible.

ops:accountant-cloud-gst.note: Needed W4 — the nearest deadline on the board. Ask it in the same conversation as the HSN questions.

ops:accountant-gst-scheme.note: Send with accountant-cloud-gst — one message, two questions; the scheme answer decides what the cloud question even means.

ops:owner-github-plan.note: Blocks server-side protection on main. Either GitHub Pro or a public repo — no third option exists.

ops:owner-delivery-hours.note: The 7am–9pm / 8am–8:30pm in Settings.dc.html are fabrications and must not survive into product.

ops:owner-font-licence.note: Cheap to ask, awkward to discover late. Either the licence permits embedding or Montserrat + DM Sans is final.

roadmap:p0-branch-protection-on-main.note: Both classic protection and rulesets return 403 on a private free-plan repo. The pre-push hook is the current substitute.

roadmap:p0-provision-dev-and-staging.note: Hosting is settled — DigitalOcean App Platform + Managed PostgreSQL in BLR1, R2 for imagery. This is the part still to do, nightly pg_dump included.

roadmap:p1-schema-products-variants-taxo.note: The approved 2026-08-18 domain design deliberately excludes the SQL schema from Phase 1 — packages/domain forbids drivers, so the rules are proven before they are persisted. Schema follows the domain package.

roadmap:p1-7-taxonomy-as-data.note: Seed generated and gated (#75), lookups shipped in packages/domain (#76). What remains is 'read by every surface' — Phase 2 onward reads the package instead of carrying literals.

case:1.12.note: Rules are tested code (#76) and the reachability half already holds; closes when a surface computes availability — schema and backend first.

case:1.17.note: Blocked on a surface: no history screen exists to re-mask, and domain rules alone cannot exercise masking.

case:1.21.note: One catalogue arrives with the real-catalogue import (Phase 2); the opaque-id-plus-slug model it maps onto shipped in #76.

case:1.30.note: Opaque ULIDs + unique slugs (#76) make the collision structurally impossible once surfaces migrate; the duplicate chip and unauthored packs close with the customer-surface port.

case:1.38.note: A delivered COD order becomes a register sale when the register reads the ledger — backend first.

case:3.6.note: The operations records agree with the README Schedule because they were copied carefully, not because anything checks. 1.46's defect, live in a new folder.
